Grace / team — quick readout from capacity: 200 tokens/sec sustained at ~15k peak is doable but depends on a few factors: model variant (float16 vs 4-bit quant), seq length distribution, and whether they use prefix caching heavily. For a single dedicated pool on A100-class hosts, expect ~180–220 tokens/sec for the curated model if we keep batching small (target latency SLO 120–180ms p50). If Pioneer wants lower latency, we'll recommend 2x capacity for headroom.

I attached a short runbook snippet with recommended batch sizes and sequence buckets. Also: ask Pioneer to provide a representative prompt set (100–200 samples) and the expected token length distribution.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-helix-v2.md (runbook excerpt)

Proposed agenda for the customer session:
- 10m: goals + success criteria (customer)
- 15m: config review (model, quant, seq dist)
- 90m: assisted test run (monitoring + quick tuning)
- 20m: readout + next steps

Availability: Aug 25 (0900–1200 PST) or Aug 26 (1300–1600 PST). If Pioneer prefers Aug 24, we can also do 1500–1700 PST but we may have less flex for tuning.

-marcus

Adding infra notes — thanks Marcus. Two technical points to highlight for the run:
1) Quantization profile: ask Pioneer whether they will accept a 4-bit quantized variant for the run. We can run FP16 but cost will be ~1.8x. If we use int4 with the Helix kernel set, we should expect slightly more variance in p95 latency; include that in the SLO conversation.
2) KV cache warmup: for sustained throughput tests, we'll run a warmup phase of ~5–10 minutes to populate per-request KV caches (unless they want cold-start behavior). That changes the effective throughput profile during the first 10 minutes — we'll flag it in the agenda.

I can lead the observability side; will bring the latency heatmap and token emission traces. I prefer Aug 25 10:00–12:00 PST. Jonas — can you confirm on-call?

Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
